# PSNES Online

> A multiplayer SNES emulator that runs in the browser. The emulation happens
> on each player's own machine — the server relays, signals and stores, and
> never runs a SNES core itself.

Two players share one deterministic machine synchronised frame by frame
(lockstep netplay), with WebRTC streaming as an alternative mode. Playing
requires signing in with Google.

ROMs are never uploaded. A game's identity — the CRC32 of its dump — is all
the server keeps; the bytes stay in the player's own browser, which is why a
library looks different from one device to the next. You must own an original
copy of any game you play here.

## Pages

- [Home](https://snes.pleymor.com/): signing in, then the library of games this
  device can actually open.

A player's profile holds their controller bindings, display and language; a
room lives under `/room/<id>` and is one session between two players. Both are
private to the player and are disallowed in
[robots.txt](https://snes.pleymor.com/robots.txt), so neither is worth
crawling.

## Source

- [pleymor/psnes-online](https://github.com/pleymor/psnes-online): the whole
  application, frontend and backend.
- [README](https://github.com/pleymor/psnes-online/blob/main/README.md): what
  it does and how the pieces fit.
- [TECHNICAL.md](https://github.com/pleymor/psnes-online/blob/main/TECHNICAL.md):
  how lockstep netplay stays in step.
